builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: RBA: A Read-out Basis Adapter for Parameter-Efficient Interactive OCTA Vessel Segmentation with SEEM
summary: RBA replaces full fine-tuning and encoder-only LoRA of the 342M-parameter SEEM model with a 0.47M-parameter adapter: 32 image-specific half-resolution basis maps at the mask read-out plus a zero-initialised projection and a rank-1 encoder LoRA, so training starts exactly from SEEM behaviour. It costs only those 0.47M trainable parameters and standard adapter training on a few hundred images, with no inference-time change beyond the added branch. It fails on the foveal avascular zone (no gain there), the 6mm result rests on a single run, and the whole result is validated only on simulated error-driven clicks on OCTA-500, so generalisation to real interactive clinical use is unproven.
rationale: This is a domain-specific adapter for interactive OCTA vessel segmentation; it is relevant only if the reader ships medical-imaging segmentation with SEEM, in which case the read-out-side adaptation insight is worth a small-scale test, otherwise it is out of scope for typical LLM production work.
technique: Read-out Basis Adapter (RBA) for SEEM segmentation

claims.statement: RBA replaces full fine-tuning and encoder-only LoRA of the 342M-parameter SEEM model with a 0.47M-parameter adapter: 32 image-specific half-resolution basis maps at the mask read-out plus a zero-initialised projection and a rank-1 encoder LoRA, so training starts exactly from SEEM behaviour. It costs only those 0.47M trainable parameters and standard adapter training on a few hundred images, with no inference-time change beyond the added branch. It fails on the foveal avascular zone (no gain there), the 6mm result rests on a single run, and the whole result is validated only on simulated error-driven clicks on OCTA-500, so generalisation to real interactive clinical use is unproven.

On OCTA-500 3mm large vessels, RBA reaches 85.16% IoU and 91.93% Dice (three-seed average), 2.90 and 1.72 percentage points above Conv-LoRA; margins of 4.35 and 2.76 points on the 6mm subset (single run).
